utterances.text: Did you return to the scene where the truck was located that evening after this meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I returned and I did as described.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say you "did as described," what exactly did you do once you were back at the scene where the truck was?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I used a green car paint spray. I thought it would match the colour of the booth. I brought two cans along, and I covered the signs on the doors. I also mounted two slightly damaged licence plates for vehicles from Bor on the front and the back of the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P600. Could we zoom in on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, is this one of the photographs that you took?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I took a negative.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What do you mean you took a negative?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I took the photograph, however that was recorded in the negative. And the photograph was developed later in Belgrade by someone at the MUP. I never developed the photographs pertaining to this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I understand. Was this photograph taken the next day after you had spray-painted the door of the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the you said the colour of the cabin was green. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a shade of green.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P603.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said that you had also put licence plates to the truck. Can we see them here in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think you can see them because they were quite damaged and there is mud on them; therefore, I really can't make them out. Perhaps on another photograph I could. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It is okay if you can't see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think one can see them here. They were placed in such a way that could be seen only by someone who would approach the truck, who would come close.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said the licence plates were covered in mud. Why was that that they had mud?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Because the workers from the electric plant who were there on the first day must have noticed that there were no licence plates; therefore, had we put new, clean licence plates, it would have been clear that someone placed them during the night. But if you put a damaged plate which had been scratched and mud placed over, then someone would probably think that they must have been there the day before except that they weren't noticeable.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who placed the mud on the licence plates?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, we see here that the hole which was visible in the previous photograph that you saw has been covered. Is this also something you did that night? It has been patched it appears on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think I did it back when the truck was first recovered and when the legs and arms started protruding. Somebody brought me some tin, screws, and a screwdriver, and I put it all back. I don't think I did that alone. I think I had some help, and I fixed it with bolts so as to avoid this crack re-appearing. The crack was a bit complicated. You could fix the bottom part but not the upper part of the crack, so I had to put some tin there. I'm sure this is tin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, was a larger crane brought the next day to try to pull the truck out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In order to recover the truck and pull it out completely, to avoid more problems with water, we brought a larger crane. And only the larger crane managed to pull out the truck all the way on to the bank. So there was no longer any danger of having the front part submerged again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that you had sent a dispatch to the Bor SUP about the truck. Did -- at any time during that day, did the district police or the staff from the Bor SUP come to Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm really not sure -- in fact, I'm convinced that they came the next day when we had already sent the dispatch describing what we had found, and the next day the large crane arrived. We ran into some problems; and then I left the scene, went to Tekija village, and called up the chief, Toma Miladinovic, to ask him if they were aware at all of what was going on in Kladovo. I know that it was around 2.00, maybe 3.00 when I called him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: On which date did this occur, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say that --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe the 7th. No. I called him on the 7th, April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say that you ran into some problems, what exactly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, some people did not show up. I realised that it was not a local problem, that we in the police department in Kladovo were not able to deal with it, that the police from Bor had to come. I don't know whether they had read our dispatch. I called the chief in Bor to ask him if he had read the dispatch, that he should go and get it and read it. I couldn't talk much because I was calling from a house, and there were other people who could overhear me. But then another chief came from the police station who said that we should suspend everything, seal everything, and wait till the chief comes from Bor with his associates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say some people did not show up, are you referring to your colleagues from the Kladovo police station, or who are you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, right. That's precisely what I meant. They did not show up, some of my colleagues. And they sent a suggestion that we should -- as to how we should deal with it, a very simple suggestion that could not solve the problem. So that is another reason why I decided to call Bor and draw their attention, because I knew that it was a job that could not be dealt with, not even at the level of the regional SUP of Bor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say that your colleagues from the Kladovo police station sent a suggestion, what are you referring to? What exactly did they suggest that you should do?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they sent a truck full of coffins, which I must say really got to me. It was really upsetting. What was I supposed to do with those coffins? Where were we supposed to carry them? But our entire region could not raise as many coffins as they had inside that truck, and I saw that there was something really wrong at our level, and that's why I called the chief of the criminal investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say that some people had not turned up, are you confining that to your colleagues, or are you thinking also of others who did not turn up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the chief of the police in Kladovo, maybe even the chief of criminal investigations who did not show up, but they sent coffins instead, as if they could be of some use. Of course not. You can't place that number of corpses into seven or eight coffins. What was I supposed to do with them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you clarify also at this stage the date when you first went with the diver to examine the lorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4th April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, after making these phone calls that you spoke about, did you return to the scene, or did you head somewhere else that evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I returned to the scene, and then a policeman came from Kladovo and told me that the chief was sending me the message to suspend all activities related to the refrigerator truck, to leave a security detail on the scene, and that I should report to him in Kladovo, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you arrived to the Kladovo police station, who else was present there, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: There was the chief of local police, Milo Stevanovic, maybe some other colleagues, but we were told that we had to wait for the chief of the SUP of Bor, Caslav Golubovic, that he was also coming with his associates and that together we'll see what we were going to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did the chief of the SUP of Bor eventually arrive that evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He did, with his colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And are you aware of whether there was a meeting between those persons present and the chief of the Bor SUP to discuss the situation about the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a meeting. Your Honour, if you allow me, I would need a short break. Just five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can go with the usher briefly, and we shall wait until you return. Thank you. I take it this is a break for comfort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, we were speaking about a meeting that was held at the Kladovo SUP. Do you know what was discussed during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting I did not attend from the very beginning. I was first at my office, and then I was called in by the chief. So I joined them, but it was only after an hour that the chief had arrived with his associates from Bor. So I don't know what they discussed previously prior to my appearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you given instructions on how to proceed regarding the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later, when I was invited to join the meeting, I reported to the chief of Bor SUP, Mr. Golubovic, about the situation on the ground, on the site. And he told me that we should organise ourselves and take the bodies out of the truck overnight.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you then return to the scene that evening or night to carry out these instructions?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Around 10.00, 11.00, we went to the scene again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you explain how you proceeded to remove the bodies from the truck.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What was the organisation like? How we used the men? What?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did you do when you returned to the scene?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: First, we did some preparatory work. We secured the necessary personnel and the funding. I went into the freight box of the refrigerator truck together with a colleague. We pulled out the bodies one by one and laid them down on the sand. Another colleague was there to take the bodies from our hands. We wrapped them in sheets. Other people came, took the bodies to the truck and loaded them, and that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How many bodies did you remove from the truck that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Thirty.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where were the bodies put once you removed them from the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were loaded on to a truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where were they taken after they were loaded on to this truck, do you know?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: All I know is that the truck left in the direction of Donji Milanovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know who was driving the truck that night, the truck on which the bodies were loaded?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was a driver from Bor, a policeman, a driver from Bor. He took the bodies away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, while you were carrying out this task of unloading the bodies from the refrigerator truck, you said that this happened at night, but did you have any type of lighting to see what -- while you were performing this task?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We only had flash-lights.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you able to observe from the bodies that you personally handled whether these were bodies of men or whether there were also women or children in the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You could see there were women, men, and two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you able to observe whether any of the bodies were dressed in any type of uniform?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody was dressed in any sort of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Based on your experience as a crime policeman, were you able to calculate for how long these bodies had been dead?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how valuable my judgement is, but I thought the bodies were not older than three or maybe four days max, if you rule out the possibility that the refrigerator truck was turned on to keep a low temperature. If it hadn't been turned on, then the bodies -- the people had met their death three or four days previously, taking into account also the temperature of the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you able to observe any type of injuries on the bodies that you handled?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were mostly dressed, but you could still see some injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What type of injuries were you able to observe on these bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, mainly from the impact of a blunt object, but also blades. In the case of blades, they were large blades, and the blunt objects used also had to be large.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you observe whether any of these bodies had gun-shot wounds?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only on one male body. There was a visible entry and exit wound in the chest because he had -- his chest was bare. He was only wearing jeans, and you could see an entry and exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about the hands of this body, this male body that you just described?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: His hands were tied with wire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, after you finished unloading these 30 bodies, did you stop for the night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were there still other bodies left in the truck when you stopped that evening, that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So did you return the next day to continue this task of unloading the bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At approximately what time the next day did you return to continue your task?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That was before noon, in daylight. In daylight, and the traffic had been stopped from Kladovo to Tekija.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, you continued unloading the bodies during the course of the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. You did not understand correctly. We stopped working, and we went home. The next day we returned in the morning and started activities to prepare for transporting the bodies from the refrigerator truck on to another lorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when did you continue your task of unloading the bodies from the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When it got dark, around 8.00, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Why did you wait until it got dark to continue with this task?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there is a populated area close by. People pass by. You had to let the traffic pass again. There is a major thoroughfare from Romania towards Kladovo. You couldn't stop traffic for the entire day. You had to let the cars pass.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How many more bodies did you unload from the truck that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Fifty-eight.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were these 58 entire bodies, or were there also body parts among this -- these bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let number -- I'm saying 58, because there were 58 heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: And about 56 -- no, it was 56, and there were three decapitated heads. So we reckoned the total, according to the number of heads. Now, as for body parts, whether there were complete bodies, whether there were more or less than 56, that was not established. There were 53 entire corpses plus three heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do your observations that you noted earlier regarding the bodies being in civilian clothes also apply to this second group of bodies that you unloaded that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you take any photographs of these bodies that were unloaded?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Why didn't you take any photographs?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, because the chief said it was not necessary; and if it should be needed, it will be done in Belgrade or some other place where the bodies are transported in the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say that the chief said it was not necessary, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean Chief Caslav, the head of the SUP of Bor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When did he give these instructions, not to take any photographs?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that evening, immediately when they came to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were other persons present when these instructions were given out?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. There were about ten of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, what happened once you finished unloading the bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the truck with the corpses also drove off towards Donji Milanovac, and the refrigerator truck that had held the bodies was hauled out and placed on a trailer; and then it was transported to Petrovo Selo, which is close to Kladovo. But I wasn't there to watch that part. I went home to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was a different truck used to transport the bodies that evening, or was it the same truck that had been used the night before with the first group of bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Another, a different truck was used that had come from Belgrade. It also had Belgrade licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the refrigerator truck at the -- that was transported to Petrovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was first incinerated, and then it was blown up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you present when this happened?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you personally carry out this task of blowing the truck up, or was someone else tasked with this?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you just responded "yes," do you mean that you personally carried out this task?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who instructed you to destroy the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Chief from Bor. Not directly Caslav Golubovic, but chief of crime police, Toma Miladinovic, because I reported to him and I -- presumably, he decided that with -- or discussed that with Caslav Golubovic, his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall the date when this occurred, when the truck was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Give me a minute to collect my thoughts. I believe that it was the 9th of April, counting 5th, 6th -- 8th or the 9th of April I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golubovic [sic], in 2001 were you strewed by a Working Group of the MUP that was tasked with investigating this incident of the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Mr. Radojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Oh, I'm very sorry, Mr. Radojkovic. That was my mistake. I'm very sorry. So, Mr. Radojkovic, in 2001 were you interviewed by a Working Group of the MUP that was tasked with investigating this incident?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you later become aware of a communique that was issued by the Working Group after your interview took place?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Your question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: After you were interviewed by this Working Group, was a communique issued by the Working Group where reference was made to the interview that you provided?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Communique addressed to whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: A communique addressed to the public, a general public information report that was issued by the Working Group.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I read this information later on. A couple days later when I went to Belgrade, I had occasion to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did the Working Group accurately transmit or communicate the information that you had provided to them some days earlier?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What was incorrect in the information that was communicated by the Working Group?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall everything, but the basic misinformation was that the refrigerator truck contained bodies wearing KLA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So do you stand by your testimony today that the bodies that you handled when you were unloading them from the refrigerator truck did not wear any type of uniform?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. All bodies in that refrigerator truck wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why it is that the Working Group incorrectly communicated this information about -- that you had provided to them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. At that time I was, pursuant to district investigative judge's order, together with MUP personnel, involved in the exhumations of the mass grave at Petrovo Selo, which is also close to Kladovo. And in those graves, apart from other bodies, there were bodies in KLA uniforms. And when the Working Group was drafting a note for the minister, Mr. Mihajlovic, they merged information about the refrigerator truck and the Petrovo Selo mass graves. They did not sort out these, and on that occasion I told them that this was inaccurate. We called the minister and corrected that and stated that the refrigerator truck contained no bodies in KLA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Kravetz. Mr. Radojkovic, you were shown a number of photographs of the truck. You had the camera from which these -- which produced these photographs. Did you, in fact, not have any of them developed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't necessary. I had the negatives in the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And was it your practice in other investigations to keep the photographs undeveloped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would depend on the case. If it is not a criminal offence, yes; but in more serious cases, photographs and studies would be produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, first will be counsel for General Lukic, and thereafter we'll follow the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, that brings were you evidence to an end. Thank you for coming here to give that evidence. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, we have now had a chance to see the joint Defence response to your application for a videolink transmission of the evidence of Dusan Loncar. Now, we have a simple question for you: Do you assure us that as far as you can tell this witness is fit to give evidence via the videolink later this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My information is that he is, Your Honour. Actually, I have scheduled to speak with him tomorrow morning, and I certainly will inquire about it at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you. We interpret the response as acknowledging that there's a measure of fragility about the health of the witness that would merit the unusual course of taking his evidence by videolink. We note also the expression of concern that the Defence have made about the witness's health. However, in this situation in an adversarial process, rather than an inquisitorial process, the onus of satisfying the Bench that the witness's condition is such as to permit him to give evidence lies with the party tendering the witness, in this case the Prosecution. We have confidence that if, as a result of the further investigation that is to be carried out just mentioned by Mr. Hannis, it is discovered that it would not be appropriate for reasons of health for the witness to give evidence layer this week, then we will be advised of that and appropriate arrangements made if we wish to check it or to postpone the evidence. But in the light of these considerations and in the state of our current knowledge, we authorise the testimony of Loncar to be given by videolink conference. Now, Mr. Hannis, does that assist with your planning of business for the rest of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it does, Your Honour. I only hope that he will be to testify on Friday, because if he doesn't I don't know who I can find to replace him. But I will not let that influence my judgement about whether or not he is indeed able and fit to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the other videolink that's arranged for Wednesday, do you anticipate that both witnesses will be completed on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honour. They're both fairly short witnesses. Even though it takes longer to do a witness by videolink, I still think in a five-hour day we can do them both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it does appear that there would be no useful purpose served by compelling you to lead your next live witness tomorrow, even if it were the afternoon, Mr. Hannis. But it is with some regret that we note that that situation has developed. So it looks as though our next sitting will be on Wednesday at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think the witness arrives at 10.00 tonight, so he'll have an extra day to rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now until 9.00 on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.18 p.m.,
